title: Colorado man dies during half-Ironman competition in Wisconsin: Report
content:
A 51-year-old Colorado man competing in a half-Ironman died Saturday after being pulled from the water during the competition in Madison, Wis.

Ironman USA Midwest announced Saturday night in a post on social media that an athlete died “after experiencing a medical emergency” during Saturday’s Ironman 70.3 Wisconsin, but organizers did not release the person’s identity, age or hometown. Madison Fire Department spokesperson Cynthia Schuster told the Wisconsin State Journal that the athlete was a 51-year-old man from Colorado. The cause of death has not been made public.

“We are deeply saddened to confirm that an athlete passed away during today’s IRONMAN 70.3 Wisconsin event after experiencing a medical emergency,” the organizers said in a statement posted to Facebook. “We extend our heartfelt condolences to the athlete’s family, friends, and loved ones during this difficult time. Out of respect for the family and the athlete’s privacy, we will have no further comment.”

Schuster, whom The Athletic couldn’t immediately reach for comment, told the State Journal that the first alert for help came in at 7:47 a.m. Firefighters and paramedics responded during the 1.2-mile swim portion of the race on Lake Monona.

Schuster told the State Journal that UW Lake Rescue had a boat on the water and brought the man ashore, where he received treatment from first responders stationed there until the paramedics and firefighters arrived. He continued to receive treatment on the way to the hospital, where he died, Schuster said.

The Ironman 70.3 is a 70.3-mile race consisting of a 56-mile bike ride, 13.1-mile run and 1.2-mile swim. A full Ironman — 140.6 miles consisting of a 112-mile bike ride, 26.2-mile run and 2.4-mile swim — was held Sunday.

The Colorado man’s death is the latest in a series of deaths in recent years connected to the Madison Ironman event, according to the Wisconsin State Journal. Among them were 51-year-old military veteran Dax Bakken, who died in the biking portion of the full competition in 2023, and two men who died after being pulled from the water during the swim portion of the Ironman 70.3 in 2019: Michael McCulloch and Todd Mahoney.
